newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sets $1 bln Nov foreign T-bill guideline.
newsitem.headline: Russia sets $1 bln Nov foreign T-bill guideline.

text.p: Russia's central bank has set a guideline of $1 billion for non-resident investment in the government securities market via S-accounts in November, first deputy chairman Sergei Aleksashenko said on Thursday.
The guideline for October was originally $1 billion too, but was raised to $1.5 billion in the face of strong foreign demand for T-bills and government bonds.

Other conditions for investing in the market were unchanged, in particular the effective guaranteed dollar yield of 16 percent for foreign investors holding securities to maturity, Aleksahenko told Reuters.
He said the investment guideline for November could also be changed if demand merited.
But in those circumstances, if demand was strong, the authorities could consider changing other conditions for non-resident investment, he said.

Since August non-residents have been able to open special rouble S-accounts at designated Russian banks. They can use roubles in these accounts to buy government securities at auction and trade them in the secondary market.
But they can only repatriate funds from the accounts through forward or option agreements with a term of at least three months.

The central bank requires commercial banks conducting these forward deals to offset 75 percent of them with the central bank at non-market rates set by the central bank -- allowing the authorities to influence the dollar return available to non-residents from investing in Russian government securities.
The authorities also control the total amount of money coming into the S-accounts each month.
